title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator
lede: Google Antigravity adds Orchestrator, which passes work back and forth between Gemini 4 Carbon for planning and Gemini 4 Hydrogen for execution inside a single agent session.

points: Carbon can explore and plan read-only, Hydrogen then edits and runs tests, and work returns to Carbon when Hydrogen gets stuck.
Google contrasts this with static routers that choose one model from the first prompt and break down on long tasks.
On Terminal-Bench 4.1 it came close to Carbon's success rate while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster.
The Antigravity SDK lets developers assign models to roles explicitly, such as Hydrogen for triage and Carbon for refactors.
Orchestrator is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers, while Pro subscribers get only the Argon variant.

points.text: Commenters compare it to Anthropic's advisor mode and GitHub's HydraFusion pipeline, and ask how caching works across models.
Several are frustrated that subscriptions only work inside each lab's own harness, so they cannot bring their own tooling.
Some are wary of letting a model decide which model gets a task; a reply argues Antigravity's value is poor enough to use Opus or GPT Sol instead.
One commenter says pairing Opus with DeepSeek Flash saves 60%, well beyond the savings Google reports.
